editorial:
Jenn wakes up on a tiny tropical island with no one around, and you feel her panic right away. The movie keeps things simple: she builds shelter, finds food, and tries to stay alive while something dangerous waits after dark. Kiersey Clemons carries almost every scene, and her fear feels real without being overdone. The island looks beautiful during the day, but that calm makes the nights feel worse. You get a tight survival story with very little talking, so the silence and small sounds do a lot of work.

The pacing is quick and never wastes time, which is great if you want a short, tense watch. The creature design is fun, though some effects look a little rough. It can feel repetitive before the final act, but the last stretch picks up fast. If you like monster movies and survival thrillers, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Jenn realizes the creature is not just hunting her; it has a nest and a pattern. After a brutal fight, she uses fire and the island’s terrain to trap and kill it. She then sees another survivor wash ashore, but the ending leaves you wondering if more creatures are nearby. It is a dark, open-ended finish that suggests her fight may not be over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creature features and solo survival stories.
